key_insight: V-PaSS uses physics-aware representations to better predict perovskite solar-cell performance for unseen absorber alloys and device architectures.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help screen new absorber compositions and transport-layer combinations beyond those represented in training data.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode device-layer sequence, cell polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: With test devices restricted to unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline; reported error reductions on unseen absorber alloys were 15.7–19.0%.
watch_item: Endpoint interpolation assumes solid-solution continuity; accuracy for compositions with phase changes or strong nonideal mixing remains to be established.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
